comparator.name: Bachelor Fiscaal Recht
comparator.sourceNotes: The current 2026–2027 Fiscaal recht OER, linked by the official ESL regulations page, controls. Articles 6, 10 and 11 and the visible PDF page 4 establish 25 unique components: 60 EC in each of three years, 180 EC overall. All previous component identities and credit weights are retained after checking the current edition. The 2026 first-year skills code is RR/RD125; obsolete RR/RD122 transitional provisions do not create an additional component. Article 4 permits full-time and part-time registration; this normalized target is full-time, Dutch-taught with the named international/EU-law assessment in English under article 5. There is no formal bachelor route to select; the generic 15-EC minor is retained under article 13, not populated for UCR convenience. A non-EUR minor requires an internally coherent package, Examination Board approval and an application eight weeks before study. Article 15 requires the skills-I evidence portfolio, completed tasks and attendance at prescribed meetings; article 16 requires all skills-II assessments and a passed Moot Court. Article 17 places research skills and the bachelor thesis within the 10-EC skills-III component, weighted 30% and 70%; the thesis requires at least 6 and the whole trajectory is mandatory. Articles 27 and 38 require the applicable first-year BSA before second-year exams. Appendix 4 requires completed B1 and at least 42 B2 EC for B3, with minor access from the third registration year even without the latter threshold. The limited 28-EC provisional skills-III entry is conditional on subsequently meeting 42 EC; it is not the normal pathway. The retained sequential 60+60+60 pathway satisfies the ordinary conditions. Old 45-EC rules in historical appendices do not control a 2026 entrant. Current public course descriptions corroborate academic content but their generic criminal-law progression and separately headed thesis are not added as extra Fiscaal recht requirements. No future course timetable or professional/master admission is guaranteed.

exception.reason: A coherent UCR programme in law, economics and public finance can be built, with genuine legal and taxation-policy contributions. It does not sustain the fiscal-legal inquiry that defines this target: interpreting tax legislation and applying it to income, profits, VAT, tax procedure and international taxing rights. Those topics organise Erasmus’s progression, skills and research, rather than merely a professional credential. The broad supporting subjects and a public-economics course therefore do not establish a sufficiently close target-level response under the current course evidence.
exception.curriculumContext: Verified complete 2026–2027 full-time Fiscaal recht pathway; 25 components, 60+60+60=180 EC, generic 15-EC approved minor and 10-EC integrated research/thesis. No external evidence blocker.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: The strongest positive argument is substantial: the closest 24-course programme contains 60 EC of real legal foundations/branches, 37.5 EC of economics including Public Economics, accounting, finance, research and rhetoric. It can implement a coherent law-and-public-finance education and genuinely addresses the societal/economic question in row 893. The failure is more specific than missing a degree label or professional qualification: the only explicit UCR taxation teaching is economic public-policy analysis, while the legal courses do not document fiscal legal interpretation, assessment/collection procedures, taxable income/profits, VAT or allocation of taxing rights. Their combination does not establish a sustained inquiry into taxation as a legal institution. Assigning fiscal projects, relabelling general EU/private law or relying on optional research would invent that missing organising link. All 35 previously selected courses were read in their actual enriched profile and description; all 151 course identities and tax/fiscal term hits were screened and six plausible additional courses read. The three mechanically feasible historical schedules are retained by immutable baseline references in the review case. No exact-equivalence rule, matching-course quota, mandatory Dutch legal system or licensing test was used.

candidateAssessment.concept: Fiscal law, legal analysis and public finance
candidateAssessment.assessment: The closest existing programme is the strongest tested response. The strongest positive argument is substantial: the closest 24-course programme contains 60 EC of real legal foundations/branches, 37.5 EC of economics including Public Economics, accounting, finance, research and rhetoric. It can implement a coherent law-and-public-finance education and genuinely addresses the societal/economic question in row 893. The failure is more specific than missing a degree label or professional qualification: the only explicit UCR taxation teaching is economic public-policy analysis, while the legal courses do not document fiscal legal interpretation, assessment/collection procedures, taxable income/profits, VAT or allocation of taxing rights. Their combination does not establish a sustained inquiry into taxation as a legal institution. Assigning fiscal projects, relabelling general EU/private law or relying on optional research would invent that missing organising link.

Company law, accounting and business organisation are real target foundations, but the proposed management/AI/strategy/market-research additions dilute the relationship to taxing business profits. Transnational business law and accounting remain genuine contributions; neither supplies the fiscal integration. It cannot repair the failed closest response.

candidateAssessment.concept: Public authority, international and European fiscal questions
candidateAssessment.assessment: Constitutional, administrative, international and EU legal foundations are substantive, but broad governance, sociology and conflict courses do not establish cross-border taxation or taxpayer procedure. Adding Public Policy Analysis improves policy study without supplying the missing fiscal-legal organising strand. No second/third alternative is exported after Alternative 1 fails.

audience.programmeDescription: Tax Law at Erasmus University Rotterdam studies how tax rules operate and how lawyers interpret and apply them. It combines Dutch, European and international taxation with public and private law, company law, accounting, public finance, legal skills and research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers law, accounting and public economics, including the economic effects of taxation. These courses support related study, but they do not provide a sustained programme in the interpretation and application of tax law. We therefore show Erasmus’s complete curriculum without presenting a UCR programme as a comparable alternative.

curriculum.limitation: The 15-EC minor is subject to access and approval rules. The 10-EC third-year legal-academic skills component includes the bachelor thesis.
